title: 갈 거예요, 할 수 있어요: -(으)ㄹ 뒤에서 세게 소리 내기
objective: You can read phrases like 갈 거예요 and 할 수 있어요 with the right tense sound.
summary: After the verb ending -(으)ㄹ, the next ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ or ㅈ is said as a tense sound, as in 갈 거예요 [갈꺼예요].

task.title: Read and say it right
task.line: Use the rule: after the verb ending -(으)ㄹ, ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ become tense; write the real sound in [ ] and say it aloud.

words.exampleMeaning: I'm going to go to school tomorrow.

words.example: 저는 한국어를 조금 할 수 있어요.
words.exampleMeaning: I can speak a little Korean.
You can see the sea from here.

letters.as: After -ㄹ, 거 becomes 꺼: a tight k, like the k in 'sky'.
After -ㄹ, 수 becomes 쑤: a sharp, strong s sound.
ㄹ ending a noun, not a verb: no change.

exercises: Write the real sound in [ ]: ① 탈 거예요 ② 쓸 수 있어요 ③ 기다릴 거예요
Does the second word start with a tense sound? Write Yes or No: ① 잘 시간 ② 마실 물 ③ 서울 사람 ④ 공부할 방
Fill in the missing sound: ① 배울 수 있어요 [배울__이써요] ② 갈 거예요 [갈__예요] ③ 살 집 [살__]
Put the words in order, then write the real sound: ① 수 / 운전할 / 있어요 ② 거예요 / 내일 / 쉴
answers: ① Yes [잘씨간] ② No [마실물] (ㅁ does not change) ③ No [서울사람] (서울 is a noun, not -(으)ㄹ) ④ Yes [공부할빵]
① 쑤 ② 꺼 ③ 찝
① 운전할 수 있어요 [운전할쑤이써요] ② 내일 쉴 거예요 [내일 쉴꺼예요]
